title: Applied: falling-object time from s = 16t^2 (rounded)

section.book: Bittinger, Beecher, Ellenbogen & Penna, College Algebra: Graphs and Models, 7e
section.title: Quadratic Equations, Functions, Zeros, and Models

sources: Example recipe in the plugin's tests (format 2); Test Form A #20 type (numbers differ)

problem.prompt: An object falls {s} ft. Using s = 16t^2, how long does the fall take? Round to three decimal places.

steps.name: take the square root of both sides (plus or minus)
throw out the answer that doesn't make sense

mistakes.name: kept the negative time
mistakes.message: A time can't be negative: keep only the positive root.

mistakes.name: didn't round
mistakes.message: The problem asks for three decimal places.

hints.why: The principle of square roots needs t^2 alone.

hints.step: take the square root of both sides (plus or minus)
hints.why: Both signs square to the same number.

hints.step: throw out the answer that doesn't make sense
hints.hint: Which answer is a negative time?
hints.why: Time is measured forward from the drop.
